_doc: Cards for the README, generated with repo-polish tools/cards/cards.py. Numbers come from indexing a 6-app project (638 files) and from a recorded Claude Code session.
title: Wiretap

hero.blurb: A live map of a codebase, from button to route to table, lit up by Claude Code's reads and edits.

demo.question: Can admins change the delivery partner?

capabilities.alt: Four things Wiretap does: map the system, show the impact of a change, watch Claude Code live, trace a feature.
capabilities.title: Four ways to look at your code.

items.title: See the whole system
items.does: Apps, backends, databases and outside services, with how many API calls and table uses link them.

items.title: Know what a change hits
items.does: Amber = what uses it, teal = what it reaches. Click a function to trace it back to the tap or route that starts it.

items.title: Watch Claude Code work
items.does: Files read, the plan, edits per function, code that calls changed code. Questions become one row per flow.

items.title: Follow a feature
items.does: Every function that uses those words, across all apps, plus functions sharing the same feature tables.

arch.alt: Architecture: the browser UI and the Claude Code terminal talk to a local Python server, which parses the codebase, keeps a cache and receives Claude Code hooks.
arch.title: One local server, two inputs.
arch.footnote: Nothing leaves your machine. Claude never reads the map; only an optional summary button calls claude -p.

flow.alt: What happens on each Claude Code tool call: hook fires, server parses it, lines map to functions, diff and ripple, push to the browser, draw.
flow.kicker: ONE CLAUDE TOOL CALL, END TO END
flow.title: From hook to picture.
steps: Claude Code runs one curl with the tool call; 1 s timeout
Read, Edit, Write, or a shell grep / sed / cat
Line ranges and grep hits become the functions they sit in
Changed functions by hash; their callers up to 3 hops
Server-sent event to every open tab
Changed files, or one row per flow for a question

decisions.alt: Design decisions: zero-token hooks, reading code instead of running it, function-level diffs, matching API calls to routes, summaries only on click.
decisions.title: Why it's built this way.
items: Hooks are a curl with a 1 s timeout that always exits 0 (wiretap/__main__.py:23). Claude never reads the map, so a slow or stopped server can't slow Claude down.
Python goes through ast, TypeScript through the compiler API without type checking. No app has to start, and a cold index of 638 files takes 1.7 s.
Each function is hashed when parsed; fn_diff (wiretap/session.py:134) compares hashes, so an edit shows as 'changed 2 functions', not a line count.
api.get/post and fetch URLs are resolved through constants, then matched to backend routes by method and path segments (wiretap/graph.py:713).
Everything on screen is computed. The one LLM call, claude -p --model haiku (wiretap/server.py:230), runs only when you press Summarize.

stack.alt: Built with Python standard library, the TypeScript compiler on Node.js, and plain JavaScript and SVG in the browser. It reads FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Supabase, React and Expo code.
stack.title: Small on purpose.

terminal.alt: Terminal: clone, npm install, copy the example config, start the server, which indexes 638 files in 1.7 seconds, then install the Claude Code hooks.
terminal.title: Running in a minute.

editor.alt: The hook command Wiretap installs: skip if WIRETAP_SKIP is set, otherwise post the hook payload with curl and a one second timeout, always exiting 0.
